root_cause.text: In `qman_destroy_fq`, the `fq_table` entry was cleared after the FQID was released back to the pool (via `gen_pool_free`), creating a race window where a concurrent `qman_create_fq` could allocate the same FQID and read a stale non-NULL `fq_table` entry.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description details the race: Thread A calls `qman_release_fqid()` (which calls `gen_pool_free()`) before setting `fq_table[fq->idx] = NULL`, allowing Thread B to allocate the same FQID and trigger `WARN_ON(fq_table[fq->idx])`. The patch fixes this by ensuring `fq_table[fq->idx] = NULL` is executed before `gen_pool_free()` (with a `smp_wmb()` barrier for ordering), as shown in the diff and comments: "To prevent that, ensure that fq_table[fq->idx] is set to NULL before gen_pool_free() is called".
